original_question: For graphs of uniform subexponential growth, specifically graphs whose growth is bounded by exp(r^c) for some 0 < c < 1, is the connected equivalence relation hyperfinite?
target_in_paper: Section 11 (Jing Yu), Problem 41: "How about graphs of uniform subexponential growth, i.e., of growth less than exp(r^c) for some 0<c<1?" Read together with the immediately preceding sentence, this is asking whether the connectedness equivalence relation of such graphs is hyperfinite. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It keeps the right growth regime, namely the paper's specific exp(r^c) bound with 0<c<1, and it correctly restores the intended conclusion about hyperfiniteness of the connected equivalence relation from the sentence immediately before Problem 41. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The Borel/descriptive-set-theoretic setting is implicit in the paper's wording here; to make the question stand-alone, one should say that G is a Borel graph on a standard Borel space X and that E_G is the equivalence relation of lying in the same connected component. Problem 41 itself suppresses this because it follows a sentence already talking about connected equivalence relations of graphs. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The graph-side countability/local-finiteness assumptions are not stated in your draft. To make sense of the connectedness relation as a countable Borel equivalence relation, one should at least impose local finiteness (or an equivalent condition ensuring finite balls). This is hidden background rather than explicit text in Problem 41. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The quantifiers in the growth hypothesis should be made explicit: there is a fixed exponent c in (0,1), and the ball-growth bound is uniform over all vertices and radii. Problem 41 states this only informally as "growth less than exp(r^c) for some 0<c<1." ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Because the paper phrases the growth condition informally, a stand-alone version should specify whether the intended bound is literal, eventual, or Big-O up to a multiplicative constant. A natural precise rendering is: there exist C>0 and c in (0,1) such that |B_G(x,r)|<=C exp(r^c) for all x and r. The paper itself does not spell out this constant/quantifier structure. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Your draft should define "hyperfinite" if it is to be fully self-contained: namely, E_G is an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations. Problem 41 assumes this background terminology from the surrounding hyperfiniteness discussion in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not be broadened to arbitrary subexponential growth given by an unspecified function f; the paper's Problem 41 keeps the narrower exp(r^c) formulation. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let G be a locally finite Borel graph on a standard Borel space X, and let E_G be its connectedness equivalence relation. Assume that G has uniform subexponential growth in the specific sense indicated in Problem 41: there exist constants C>0 and c in (0,1) such that for every x in X and every r in N, the ball B_G(x,r) has size at most C exp(r^c). Must E_G be hyperfinite; equivalently, is E_G an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 41 in Section 11, not the broader Weiss question in Problem 40. The paper first recalls known hyperfiniteness results for connected equivalence relations of graphs of polynomial growth and for graphs of growth less than exp(r^c) for some sufficiently small 0<c<1, and then asks the next-step question: "How about graphs of uniform subexponential growth, i.e., of growth less than exp(r^c) for some 0<c<1?" Because Problem 41 omits the words "connected equivalence relation" and "hyperfinite," a faithful stand-alone rewrite must restore those from the immediately preceding sentence, while keeping the paper's narrower exp(r^c) growth condition and not broadening it to arbitrary subexponential functions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
